clue.text: A blow husband losing hair? On the contrary

indicators.note: losing says one piece is taken away from another, leaving the rest
on the contrary swaps the roles: it is the hair that loses the husband, not the other way round

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A punch, perhaps, or a husband going bald? No, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue wants hair taken from a husband; 'On the contrary' turns it round, so H is removed from SHOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is slang for a punch or hard hit, so it is a blow.

clue.text: One used to call them aprons, originally

indicators.note: originally says these letters were once in another order, so the words them aprons are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone once used to call people in aprons by this name, back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is an unusual anagram signal: the answer's letters were originally THEM APRONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartphone is a mobile device people use for making calls.

clue.text: Dig hard for convincing Wimbledon success?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or loving it
set means hardened, as concrete or jelly sets hard

explanation.surface: Advice to dig in and work hard for a good result in the tennis at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means zero, so a love set is one won six games to nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis set won without the loser taking a single game is a convincing, one-sided victory.

clue.text: Got to call for guide — with no answer

parts.note: to call for something is to need it

indicators.note: with no says a letter is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: to guide is to lead

explanation.surface: Someone had to call for a guide, without getting any reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got to' looks like 'had to', but it is the informal sense of being got at, irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: If something got to you it annoyed you; needled likewise means irritated or provoked.

clue.text: Insulting about excursion that Tube provides?

indicators.note: about says one word goes round another

parts.note: slighting means insulting or snubbing
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: Rude remarks about a day out that the London Underground laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Tube' look like the London Underground, but it is a fluorescent tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Strip lighting is the long fluorescent tube type of lamp, so a tube provides it.

clue.text: Double helping of caramel pudding sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request for a second portion of caramel pudding returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double helping' reads as a big portion; 'helping' is only a link and 'Double' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple time in music has two beats to the bar, so duple means double or twofold.

clue.text: Artist in Arundel upset clergyman

indicators.note: in says the artist's letters go inside the town's name before the shake-up
upset says the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter in the Sussex town of Arundel annoyed a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a small historic town in West Sussex, England, with a famous castle; the clergyman is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England priest who supervises a group of parishes, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Surprisingly ok with Conservative re attitude to Labour

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters fall in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, the Tories are fine with a view about the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with a capital looks like the British political party, but it just means work.
explanation.definitionFit: A work ethic is a person's attitude to work, a belief in the value of hard toil.

clue.text: One of two comperes introducing a single entertainer

indicators.note: introducing says one piece is brought into the middle of the other

parts.note: a co-host sharing the role is a co-MC, MC being master of ceremonies
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

explanation.surface: One of a pair of hosts brings on a solo performer.
explanation.walkthrough: MC is master of ceremonies; the co-host is CO-MC, and the single I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a comedian, a stand-up performer who entertains audiences.

clue.text: One of a pair at 5 into rambling helping celebrate tours

indicators.note: tours says the outer pieces travel round the inner one

parts.note: a quota is a share or helping
to mark an occasion is to celebrate it

indicators.note: rambling says the letters wander into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A walking holiday that marks a celebration with tours of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue at 5 down prints "arm" between a pair of inverted commas, so the definition points there. 'rambling' signals the anagram and 'tours' the surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks come in pairs, and the clue at 5 down prints one on each side of a word.

clue.text: Very dull when one is followed by several more

indicators.note: followed by puts the next piece after the previous one

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
I is the Roman numeral for one
nine is several more than the one already given

explanation.surface: Something that grows tedious when one item is trailed by plenty more.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid like a donkey, and dull can mean slow-witted.

clue.text: Grouse a lot, endlessly cross

parts.note: to beef is to grouse or complain

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone moans a great deal, angry without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid of domestic cattle and bison, so a cross between breeds.

clue.text: Bungling one exposed penning page in French and Italian

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: penning says the outer word encloses the others like a pen

parts.note: nude means exposed or bare

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the French word

parts.note: et is the French word for and
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A clumsy person is left exposed while writing a page in French and Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is clumsiness or incompetence, the quality behind bungling.

clue.text: Sat in this, worn out, for audition

indicators.note: for audition says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: weak means feeble, worn out

explanation.surface: Someone sat through an exhausting audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is not the verb but short for Saturday, a day in every seven-day period.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday is one of the seven days in each calendar week.

clue.text: The main landing has prominent feature, blue

parts.note: a splash is a prominent feature, like a front-page splash
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: The chief stair landing boasts an eye-catching blue feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, so its landing is a spacecraft coming down on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a spacecraft landing in the sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: In vessel there's extra whitewash

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
over means extra or left over

explanation.surface: Inside the container there is surplus paint for whitewashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover-up hides wrongdoing, which is what a whitewash does figuratively.

clue.text: Top female pilot losing tail section in border territory

indicators.note: in says the shortened word goes inside the other

parts.note: a march is a frontier district, as in the Welsh Marches

indicators.note: losing tail section says the final letter goes

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a trial

explanation.surface: A leading woman pilot loses part of her plane's tail over contested border land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' suggests an aviator, which 'tail section' encourages; it is a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the woman who heads a family or group, its top female.

clue.text: Farm? That's "arm", wanting head

indicators.note: wanting head says the first letter is missing

parts.note: a branch is an arm, of a tree or an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a farm is really just an arm missing its first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tempts you to remove F from 'Farm' to get ARM; instead arm means BRANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle in North America.

clue.text: A letter for the linesman?

parts.note: a linesman here is a writer of verse lines, and a letter is a written permit or licence granting freedom

explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom allowed to writers of verse to bend rules, a permit for poets.

clue.text: Please tip for service: we owe him

parts.note: to oblige someone is to please them

indicators.note: tip for picks the end letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A diner's note asking for a tip for good service, saying what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip for service' looks like a gratuity; it is the last letter of 'service'.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligee is the person to whom an obligation or debt is owed.

clue.text: Tips accompanying the odds?

definitions.meaning: the phrase odds and ... puts this word alongside odds

explanation.definitionFit: Ends are tips of things, and they go with odds in the phrase for miscellaneous scraps.

clue.text: Communist leaders presume vote is rigged

indicators.note: rigged says the letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The party bosses take it for granted that the ballot is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supreme Soviet was the highest legislative body of the USSR, its Communist leadership.

clue.text: Sort of policy not allowing for jokey introduction

indicators.note: not allowing says a word is removed from the longer phrase

parts.note: knock-for-knock is a motor insurance arrangement where each insurer pays its own client
taken as written

explanation.surface: A type of insurance policy that does not cover something, introduced as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock-for-knock agreement is a British insurance term where insurers each pay their own customer's claim regardless of fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-knock joke opens with that formula, so it is a jokey introduction.

clue.text: Leisure facility supplied with members, grew again?

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground or centre
limbed means having limbs, which are members of the body

explanation.surface: A sports centre has gained new members and has grown once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests club membership; here members are limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant grows upward, so to have climbed again is, whimsically, to have grown again.

clue.text: Make note on paper

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a memo down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' reads as create, but it means compel, as in 'make him go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To require someone to do something is to oblige or compel them, to make them.

clue.text: Brief encounter involves a duty to produce murder weapon?

indicators.note: involves says the shortened word wraps round the others
brief says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to meet is to encounter
a tax is a duty

explanation.surface: A short meeting involving a tax bill results in a killing weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief Encounter' is a famous British film, a deliberate red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat axe is a butcher's cleaver, which could serve as a murder weapon.

clue.text: Lille's wingers with all-round skill on the ball

indicators.note: with all-round says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: wingers are the outermost players, so the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Lille's wide players, with their all-round skill on the ball, as in football.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is French football; 'on the ball' means alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the ball is quick and attentive, which is what alert means.

clue.text: Skirt mum removed from ceiling

indicators.note: removed from says one word is taken out of another

parts.note: a ceiling is an upper limit or maximum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother's skirt was taken down from the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long skirt reaching the ankles.
